principle: Design the instructions, materials, tool descriptions and conversation history the model reads. Retrieve or compress information when needed; reduce outdated or irrelevant material.
example: For a product manual revision, first supply the current specification and relevant tests. Retrieve earlier versions only when needed.
verify: Use fixed questions to compare evidence coverage, irrelevant context and outdated versions.

principle: Design the execution environment, tools, permissions, tests and feedback outside the model. A harness describes the surrounding execution and verification structure, not a single standard.
example: Give a documentation agent a separate branch, allowed write paths, linting, tests and stop conditions for failures. Do not grant production merge permission.
verify: Test blocked writes, stopping merges on failed tests and reproducibility with identical input. Do not rely on instruction files alone.

principle: Package procedures and references for repeated tasks. The Agent Skills specification uses SKILL.md for name, description and instructions, with optional resources or scripts.
example: A meeting-notes skill specifies inputs, extraction of decisions, owners and deadlines, and examples. Mark owners absent from the source as undecided.
verify: Test fictional meeting notes for consistent structure, handling missing information and not using the skill when irrelevant.

principle: A handler responds to an execution event. Claude Code supports events and matchers such as PreToolUse and PostToolUse. Behavior and blocking depend on product and event.
example: Check allowed paths before editing and run formatting checks afterward. Log failures for human investigation.
verify: Test allowed and forbidden paths, matcher mismatches, error exits and timeouts. Do not treat hooks as the sole security boundary.

principle: A Markdown file providing project instructions to Claude Code sessions. Persistent instructions and automatic memory differ; check documentation for path-specific rule scope.
example: At the repository root, specify build commands, edit scope and tests, linking detailed rules.
verify: Check fresh-session recognition and enforce forbidden operations through permissions and CI. Never include secrets.

principle: Markdown instructions describing how supported coding agents work on a project. Unlike a human-facing README, discovery scope and priority vary by tool.
example: Document install and test commands, conventions, validation criteria and related documents. Add subproject instructions where supported.
verify: Check correct test commands and scope in new tasks. Check for mismatches between instructions and CI.
